newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa rallies but ends off highs.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa rallies but ends off highs.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures finished off highs on Thursday after a speculative short-covering rally ran out of gas, traders said.

A strong close in New York on Wednesday encouraged fund buyers early on, dragging the benchmark March contract to a high of 1,019 stg. But several attempts to vault that level faltered as it ran into origin selling and profit taking.
Traders noted a continuous flow of cocoa from Ivory Coast and Nigeria sold onto middle positions but these were well absorbed throughout the session.
"We can see the market inching up to 1,025. When it gets there we'll see how much resistance there is," said one.
March ended nine stg higher at 1,014 stg, but activity centred mainly on switches with May 97/May 98 trading at between 58 and 55 stg. Volume was brisk at 12,675 lots.

Optimism was buoyed on Wednesday after news that German third quarter grind increased by a healthy seven percent to 65,824 tonnes. This confirmed a strong trend that emerged in the rest of Europe last week.
The next grind data on the line is from the United States, possibly next week. According to brokers GNI, an increase could lead to a big upward revision to demand in 1996/97.
Traders said Thursday's rally could have featured some fresh buying, which would be apparent in open interest figures on Friday.
